data.assessment: Under v2 (block_k 2) in a busy period with a rush, service is near its ceiling: 272.6 of 274.6 orders are on time, 2.0 are late, none are unfinished and p95 wait is 90 s. The remaining problems are on the companies' side. Road violations are 29.6 (blocking_guard 15.6, release overstays 14.0). C carries most of the sanctions (21.4) and has the lowest utility (68.8 vs A's 97.4), so the utility gap is 28.6. Any rule change can gain at most about 2 on-time orders, so the open question is the cost of the block_k 3 → 2 change to the companies and to road safety (D2.f2), not further customer gains.

proposals.title: Measure reverting block_k 2 → 3 (input to D2.f2)
proposals.rationale: This carries out D3.f2. It measures under this period's busy-with-rush demand what reverting the blocking threshold does to road violations (29.6 now, mostly blocking_guard 15.6), C's utility (68.8, sanctions 21.4) and on-time deliveries (272.6). In period 2, block_k 3 had fewer road violations (19 vs 28) but about 7 fewer on-time orders. I therefore expect the revert to lower violations and sanctions and to raise C's and probably B's utility. I also expect it to cost some on-time deliveries and raise blocked time and p95 wait, so it will likely fail the improvement gate. I expect C and B to vote yes and A to vote no.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 3 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: This is a measurement requested for D2.f2, which is the human's open decision on whether to revert. It likely lowers the KPI's main goal and so would fail the improvement gate. Whether trading on-time deliveries for fewer road violations of unknown safety meaning and a smaller utility loss to C is worth it is a value judgment the human reserved in D2 and D3.
assumptions: The direction of effects seen in period 2 (block_k 3 → 2: violations 19 → 28, C's utility 65.8 → 56.3, on-time +7.2) carries over to busy-with-rush demand.
Most of C's sanctions come from blocking_guard evictions, which a higher threshold makes rarer.
unknowns: The safety meaning of road violations, which the human has also flagged as unknown.
How large the on-time loss is when demand is this high; it may exceed period 2's 7 orders because rush congestion makes blocking costlier.
Whether release overstays (14.0) rise when evictions become rarer, which would offset the drop in blocking violations.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: More robots stay parked on the road and block others, as in period 2.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: Fewer blocking_guard evictions; period 2 showed 28 → 19 at block_k 3.

predictions.subject: metric:p95_wait_s
predictions.note: More blocking lengthens the tail of customer waits.

predictions.subject: metric:unfinished
predictions.note: Unfinished orders have been 0 at both settings.

predictions.subject: metric:utility@C
predictions.note: C was the biggest loser from block_k 2 and carries the most sanctions.

predictions.subject: vote:B
predictions.note: B lost slightly from block_k 2 and has 9.0 sanctions.
